title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Visually checked ventricular peaks and measured R–R intervals in original PDF 500
fields.reason: R–R intervals: 1.301 s, 1.26 s, 1.22 s, 1.236 s. These describe the short displayed sample, not an independently adjudicated rhythm diagnosis.

fields.basis: Assumed course speed of 25 mm/s; independently checked 150 small-square intervals across 738 pixels
fields.reason: Mean R–R estimate 47.8 bpm; six-second count estimate 50 bpm. These methods differ with phase at the strip endpoints, especially for irregular rhythms. The strip itself has no printed paper-speed label.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Repeated small upright deflections precede five QRS complexes, separated from the preceding broad post-QRS wave by a long nearly level segment. Candidate P identity is supported by repetition and temporal separation, not by a sinus label.

fields.basis: Original PDF page 500; independently reconciled endpoint bands and horizontal grid; assumes course 25 mm/s (0.04 s per small square), not a verified per-strip speed
fields.reason: Conditional on the repeated isolated candidates being P waves; endpoint bounds include manual placement uncertainty. Approximate reader-union envelope, conditional on course speed and candidate P identity. This envelope includes reader and endpoint uncertainty; it is not a confidence interval, normal/abnormal classification, or proof of beat-to-beat physiological variation.

fields.value: Slow near-regular ventricular spacing over this short strip, with a conditional mean rate near 48 bpm and separate P-like lobes before the five complexes. Sinus bradycardia remains a hypothesis requiring confirmation of uniform sinus P waves and a consistent 1:1 P-QRS relationship. The conditional PR range crosses 0.20 s and QRS end is unresolved, so normal conduction is not established.

fields.reason: Any named rhythm is a conditional teaching hypothesis, not an assigned diagnosis or scored answer. limitations: New wave-field estimates remain provisional and unscored. Range width reflects uncertain endpoints and reader disagreement, not a validated diagnostic category. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established.
The exact original PDF was checked. The inspected waveforms are embedded rasters; larger rendering does not add samples. Expert interpretation may still improve unresolved component identification.

QRS duration unresolved: Terminal S recovery merges with notched depressed segment; an early knee versus a later shoulder changes the QRS end. Preserve uncertainty and do not assert normal conduction.
Calibration assumes the course’s 25 mm/s convention (PDF pages 228, 230, 231 and 234). Every image grid was checked separately; the assumption is not a per-strip speed label.
Peak positions are approximate to about ±2 source pixels; morphology, low-amplitude P waves and boundaries remain uncertain. This is not a statistical confidence interval.
